items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: We had sets with Dave McKenna and Dick Hyman, Antti Sarpila, we had wonderful people.

ctx.x: Yeah. We had an earlier conversation about the importance placed on jazz in this country and abroad. Does it make a difference when you go overseas to play, in the response?

Yes it does. Less than it used to, because I think that now it’s become commonplace. American musicians are appearing on the doorstep just about every other day. And it’s been known for certain musicians from the United States to appear twice in our little country in England. And they are not necessarily filling halls, they’re working in small © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

pubs and places like that. It’s beneath them, beneath their talent, and I don’t approve of them having to do that. But unfortunately it’s the only way. If you want to do two tours a year you can’t do them both in concert halls you see? I think that now the message has gotten out, and certainly some of the Swedish are brilliant players.
